extraction_metadata.notes: On September 16, 2026 the FDA awarded Cognita Imaging a $1.29M research contract to build an 'LLMs-as-a-jury' system for evaluating radiology reports — multiple LLM agents cross-examining AI-generated reports. Directly relevant to the interpretability-vs-certification theorem card and to multi-agent verification architectures.

title: FDA funds an 'LLMs-as-a-jury' system for evaluating radiology reports
subtitle_or_tagline: Cognita Imaging wins $1.29M contract — multiple LLM agents cross-examine AI-generated radiology reports
topic: The FDA awarded Cognita Imaging a $1.29 million research contract (September 2026) to build what the company calls an 'LLMs-as-a-jury' evaluation system: multiple large language model agents independently assess AI-generated radiology reports, then their verdicts are aggregated like jury votes. This is regulatory-grade multi-agent verification — the insight being that a single model's self-assessment is unreliable, but a diverse ensemble of independent evaluators cross-examining the same artifact converges toward trustworthy judgment.

components.name: LLM Jurors (ensemble)
components.role: Multiple independent LLM agents, each assessing the report

components.name: Jury Aggregation
components.role: Combines individual verdicts into a calibrated final assessment

components.name: Human Oversight
components.role: Regulatory reviewers receive aggregated evidence, not raw output

architecture.data_flow: AI-generated report -> N independent LLM jurors -> verdict aggregation -> regulatory-grade assessment

workflow_steps: Step 1 - An AI system generates a draft radiology report
Step 2 - Multiple independent LLM agents each review the report against clinical criteria
Step 3 - Each juror produces an independent verdict (like jury deliberation)
Step 4 - Verdicts are aggregated; disagreement is surfaced as a signal
Step 5 - Aggregated assessment feeds regulatory review workflow
key_claims: Multi-agent jury architecture replaces single-model self-evaluation
Designed for regulatory-grade assessment of AI-generated reports
Independent cross-examination surfaces hallucinations single reviewers miss
Signals FDA's interest in ensemble-verification patterns for AI oversight
caveats_or_warnings: LLM jurors are themselves language models — correlated failure modes are possible
A research contract is not a regulatory mandate yet
Jury aggregation requires careful design to avoid bias amplification
osiris_connection: LLMs-as-a-jury is statistical certification: N independent evaluators bound the error rate of the whole ensemble. OSIRIS's Theorem 7 is mathematical certification: the norm-clamp bounds the displacement of every update, so total drift is bounded by L*c. The jury answers 'is this report likely wrong?' with a probability; the norm-clamp answers 'can this update ever produce an unbounded artifact?' with a proof. The FDA funding both kinds of verification in the same month (DeepHealth's foundation-model clearance, Cognita's LLM jury) shows the regulatory world converging on what OSIRIS formalizes: no single evaluation is sufficient — you need bounded updates AND independent verification.
